flows: Cron views and view models call CronCategory split/name helpers to derive categories, groupings, and labels from job names
responsibilities: Derive cron category paths from job names as a pure naming convention
Normalize and validate user-typed job names so renaming is also refiling
Own value-oriented wire and domain types shared across experiences and service adapters
Provide shared display-name rules so list rows, cards, and graph labels cannot drift apart
components.summary: Value types and wire/domain models shared across user experiences and service adapters. Cron job organization is modeled here: CronCategory derives arbitrary-depth category paths from a job's own name (life/training/morning-run) with no schema change, and owns the display-name rules shared by every surface — displayName(for:showingPath:) drops the whole path for tree rows whose headers are the path, while name(_:strippingLeadingFolder:) drops only the leading folder for the interflow graph's hull labels so deeper levels stay visible.

flows: graph didSet refreshes hulledCategoryFolders from categoryHulls; the canvas asks displayLabel(forKind:label:) per node when drawing labels
responsibilities: Cache hulled category folders on graph change so per-frame label drawing avoids walking every node
Expose category hulls for cron folders with two or more jobs as a visual grouping with stable tints
Own observable state machines for operations surfaces: sessions, cron, activity, feed, skills, settings, gateway lifecycle, learning, and the file browser
Resolve per-node canvas labels: strip the hull's folder when the hull already names it, keep the full name otherwise
components.summary: Session, cron, activity, feed, skill, settings, gateway-lifecycle, learning, and file-browser state machines. CronGraphViewModel drives the interflow graph simulation: categoryHulls groups cron nodes by top-level folder (folders with two or more jobs), the hulled folders are cached in hulledCategoryFolders whenever the published graph changes, and displayLabel(forKind:label:) resolves the canvas text for a node — a cron inside a hull gets its leading folder stripped because the hull already names it, while ungrouped or single-job-folder crons keep their full name.

flows: CronGraphCanvas.drawHullLabels draws each category folder above its hull; drawLabels asks the view model for each node's display label
responsibilities: Draw category hulls and their uppercased folder labels above clustered cron nodes in the interflow canvas
Present the operations surfaces: sessions, cron, activity, skills, learning, mission control, and the Hermes file browser
Resolve node label text through the view model rather than duplicating the strip rule in the canvas
components.summary: Sessions, cron, activity, skills, learning, mission-control, and the read-only Hermes file browser. In the cron interflow canvas (CronGraphCanvas), each category hull draws its folder name uppercased in 9pt bold above the cluster, and node labels are resolved through the view model's displayLabel(forKind:label:) instead of restating the strip rule in the view, so a cron inside a hull never repeats the folder the hull already names.
